name: Pentafall (rebuild)
statusNote: Under active development, not published: core slices (spine, feel, threat, damage model) complete with 485 automated tests green; build-craft, destination, and content slices partial; polish/ship not started.
oneLiner: A ground-up rebuild of pentafall — a deadpan megacorp-satire wave-survival roguelite: a momentum ship with auto-firing turrets, draft-based leveling, escalating bosses, and a full between-run meta-economy.
stack: hand-rolled Canvas 2D engine, no WebGL, no physics libraries

components.name: bridge.js
components.desc: A ~19-line event bus — the only seam between the vanilla-JS engine and the React shell.

components.name: game.js + loop.js
components.desc: Owns input and four named scene pipelines; a fixed-timestep loop wrapped in try/catch/finally so a thrown error re-arms rAF instead of freezing.

components.name: world.js
components.desc: Single state container with documented reset-parity guarantees.

components.name: Systems
components.desc: Flight, spawn director, enemy AI (9 movement archetypes), turrets, combat damage pipeline with a hard global 10x ceiling, hazards, fighters, progression, autopilot, drydock.

components.name: Data tables
components.desc: ~30 weapons, a 5-type elemental RPS wheel, two-tree evolutions, cards, 4 hulls, 3 boss fights, 7 champion affixes, 30 meta-store glyphs, 6 doctrines.

components.name: renderer.js
components.desc: ~1053 lines of fully procedural pixel-art rendering — flagged as the largest file and a split candidate.

components.name: React UI + persistence
components.desc: Menus, HUD, 3 save slots, and audio policy — persistence lives entirely in the UI layer, never the engine.

components.name: Electron wrapper
components.desc: electron-builder portable Windows build for Steam distribution.

dataFlow: Player input feeds the active scene's pipeline each tick: flight, spawn director, enemy AI, turret auto-targeting and fire, fighter AI.
Combat resolves through the damage pipeline and a single killEnemy funnel that drops loot and XP gems.
Foe shots, asteroids, black holes, and singularity hazards run their physics.
XP pickup pauses the world at level-up and opens a 3-card draft.
renderer.js draws the frame; bridge.js emits a stats event and the React HUD re-renders.
React intents (restart, pick card, buy glyph) flow back through the bridge into engine mutations.
Attract mode substitutes the autopilot system for player input into the identical pipeline.
integrations: Parts-donor engine for the Boat-Rogue design
decisions: The damage model is hard-capped by construction — a global 10x ceiling makes runaway power-scaling structurally impossible.
First death is the tutorial: the first loss reframes as the shift ending and opens the store in the death panel.
Determinism is a contract — fixed-seed tests assert byte-identical results across 3 seeds, plus committed outcome fixtures.
Ship via an Electron wrap, not a rewrite — a 3-agent audit concluded stay on vanilla JS.
Known design debt is tracked honestly: meta-progression currently leans harder on flat power than intended, and reduced-motion coverage is flagged as a must-fix gap.
Persistence never touches the engine — save slots and audio settings live in the React layer.
